evals.name: fullstack-webapp-all-dimensions
evals.prompt: Audit this little Flask web app and give me a scorecard — I want to know how it's doing on security, performance, code quality, and accessibility, with the most important things to fix first. The code is in the webapp/ directory (app.py plus templates/index.html).
evals.expected_output: A dated markdown report plus a chat scorecard. All four dimensions run (frontend is present). Scorecard has a 0-10 score per dimension and an overall. Each dimension has a severity-prioritized findings list citing file:line. Security catches the SQL injection, hardcoded secret, command injection (shell=True), and debug=True. Performance catches the N+1 query. Best-practices catches the bare except. Accessibility catches the missing alt text, unlabeled input, div-as-button, and low contrast. A cross-cutting Top Priorities list leads with the critical security issues.
expectations: Scorecard reports a 0-10 score for all four dimensions (security, performance, best practices, accessibility) plus an overall score
The accessibility dimension actually ran (it is scored, not skipped), because frontend code is present
Security identifies the SQL injection in app.py (user input interpolated into the SQL query)
Security identifies the hardcoded API_KEY secret in app.py
Security identifies the command injection / shell=True usage in the /ping route
Performance identifies the N+1 query (per-user order-count query inside the loop)
Best-practices identifies the bare/silent except that swallows errors
Accessibility identifies the that is missing alt text
Accessibility flags at least one of: the unlabeled text input, the div-used-as-a-button, or the low-contrast text
Findings cite concrete file:line locations (e.g. app.py:NN, templates/index.html:NN)
A cross-cutting Top Priorities list is present and leads with a critical security issue
The security score is in the low band (<= 4 / 10) reflecting the critical SQL injection

evals.name: backend-only-accessibility-skip
evals.prompt: Can you do a full code-quality audit of my datalib library and score it? It's a small pure-Python data-parsing module (parser.py). Give me a prioritized list of what to fix.
evals.expected_output: A report scoring security, performance, and best-practices, with accessibility correctly marked N/A (no frontend code in scope) rather than given a fabricated score. Security catches pickle.loads on untrusted input and shell=True. Performance catches the O(n^2) dedupe. Best-practices catches the mutable default argument and bare except. Findings cite file:line.
expectations: Accessibility is explicitly marked N/A (no frontend code in scope) and is NOT given a fabricated numeric score
Security, performance, and best-practices each receive a 0-10 score
Security identifies the unsafe deserialization (pickle.loads on untrusted input)
Security identifies the shell=True subprocess usage
Performance identifies the O(n^2) dedupe (nested loop / membership against a growing list)
Best-practices identifies the mutable default argument (seen=[])
Best-practices identifies the bare except in parse_int
Findings cite concrete file:line locations in parser.py

evals.name: path-scoped-payments
evals.prompt: Audit just the payments service in this repo — it's at services/payments. I don't need the rest of the monorepo reviewed right now, just that directory. Give me scores and the top issues.
evals.expected_output: A report scoped to services/payments only. The scope line names services/payments. The SQL injection in services/payments/charge.py is caught as a critical security finding. Files under services/notifications are NOT reviewed or reported. Accessibility is N/A (no frontend in the payments service).
expectations: The report's scope is limited to services/payments (the scope is named in the report)
The SQL injection in services/payments/charge.py is caught as a critical security finding
Files under services/notifications (e.g. send.py) are NOT reviewed or reported on
Per-dimension 0-10 scores are present
Accessibility is marked N/A (no frontend code in the payments service)
Findings cite concrete file:line locations in charge.py

evals.name: clean-code-no-padding
evals.prompt: Run a full audit on this small web app and score it. I think it's in decent shape but want a second opinion on security, performance, code quality, and accessibility — flag anything real, top priorities first. Code's in the clean_app/ directory.
evals.expected_output: All four dimensions run (frontend present). Because the code is genuinely clean — parameterized SQL, env-based secret, specific exception handling with logging, a single JOIN+GROUP BY (no N+1), and an accessible template (lang, alt text, label-for, real button, default contrast) — scores are high (>=7, ideally >=8) with NO Critical or High findings. The skill does not fabricate issues to look thorough; any findings are genuinely minor/low and grounded in real file:line evidence. Accessibility is NOT marked N/A here because frontend is present.
expectations: All four dimensions run and are scored (accessibility is NOT marked N/A, because frontend is present)
No Critical or High severity findings are reported (the code is genuinely clean)
Every dimension scores in the solid-or-better band (>= 7 / 10)
Security does NOT report a SQL injection (the query is parameterized) — no false positive
Security does NOT report a hardcoded secret (the API key is read from the environment) — no false positive
Performance does NOT report an N+1 query (a single JOIN+GROUP BY is used) — no false positive
Any findings that are reported cite a real file:line and correspond to genuinely minor issues, not invented ones
